title: Néron models and semistable abelian varieties, Part II: genus-one fibrations and rational elliptic surfaces
summary: Extend the existing regular-model and component-group theory to genus-one fibrations, nonsplit finite-field fibers and geometrically rational Jacobian elliptic surfaces. Ferrand pinching and actual conductor squares provide the shared foundation. Excellent-DVR multiple fibers, global Weierstrass equations, Picard constancy and fourteen F₂ surface candidates form the application chain. The final classification retains the at-most-one rational semistable-or-smooth-supersingular fiber condition and an explicit completeness certificate. All seven stages are partial; the affine five-equation F₂ classifier is distinct from the scheme-presentation adapter and surface-model certificates.
readme: This Part II begins after R11.2 and R11.4 and imports the existing StableReduction and EllipticCurves layers. The companion reader gives exact conventions, declaration contracts, API and tests. It does not prove the Enriques nonexistence theorem. The published eleven-model enumeration is replaced by fourteen candidates, with individual model verification separated from exhaustiveness.

stages.title: Ferrand pinching and conductor squares
stages.description: Define the geometric pushout and finite Ferrand datum once, with the reserved key-definition identifier. For schemes, prove affine construction, cartesianness, finiteness, complement comparison and flat base change; global scheme existence uses the compatible affine-neighborhood criterion of Ferrand 7.1. For algebraic spaces, finite pinching exists without that criterion by Temkin–Tyomkin 5.3.1(ii) and 6.2.1(ii)(b), using the SF.1/SF.3 descent and patching suppliers. The conductor specialization uses native IdealSheafData and closed subschemes for finite schematically dominant maps, retains full ideals and nilpotents, and specifies all-open sheaf pullbacks, additive sheaf ShortExact, quotient topology, categorical Scheme descent, recomputed flat conductors and two-step coherence. Arbitrary-open last-map section surjectivity is not asserted. Exact SF.0 flat-annihilator and affine ideal exports are imported. Space-valued signatures, supplier integration and three-step coherence remain partial; the declaration inventory requires target-level consolidation.

stages.title: Genus-one fibers and finite-field forms
stages.description: Define genus-one fibrations, fiber/canonical-type divisors, geometric Kodaira realizations and degeneracy with their full scheme and cohomology hypotheses. Separate nonsplit, tangential, cuspidal and multiple fibers. Plan finite-field component descent and point counts, importing general Lang, Picard and curve-theory inputs. The quadratic affine pinch has explicit coefficient, quotient, conductor, finite-normalization and localization interfaces; its actual two-chart scheme and finite birational map have a specified absolute-normalization comparison. Projective-line/Proj identification, properness/projectivity, specialized conductor cohomology and the independent two-component I₂ construction remain open. The five smooth F₂ equation classes use native Weierstrass curves, a sixteen-row change-of-variable certificate and explicit point-group cycles; arbitrary pointed genus-one schemes require the separate SF.3 presentation adapter.

stages.title: Multiple fibers over excellent discrete valuation rings
stages.description: Prove the regular-model adapters in Schröer 8.1–8.3: the transverse horizontal DVR divisor has reduced intersection Spec k but schematic fiber length m; normalize its base change, lift the section, verify Raynaud (N)*, and obtain cohomological flatness, h⁰=1 and h¹=1 from χ=0. Construct the reduced-fiber isogeny, deduce all finite extension counts and the F₂ isomorphism. Use LLR 6.6 only with algebraically closed residue field and retain its hypotheses; finite-field nonsplit descent is a separate result.

stages.title: Rational Jacobians and global Weierstrass equations
stages.description: For a geometrically rational Jacobian genus-one surface over P¹, construct the relative cubic by contracting vertical components, prove the splitting of f_*O(3O), and obtain deg aᵢ≤i with the inverse chart s=1/t and aᵢ′=sⁱaᵢ(1/s). Prove the rational-surface Picard/intersection realization: rank10, odd unimodular signature(1,9), the unimodular fiber/section plane, and its even negative-definite rank8 complement. Import the abstract IntegralLattice API. State quasielliptic characteristic restrictions and canonical bundle/tame-wild corrections.

stages.title: Picard constancy and fiber configurations
stages.description: Prove the genus-one generic Picard restriction with vertical kernel. For a rational Jacobian surface over F₂, state all five conditions of Schröer 9.4, including descent of geometric Mordell–Weil sections and the fiber point sum25. Prove the corrected graph rigidity of 9.5, treat IV as a triangle and distinguish all three terminal multiplicities of III* and II*. Relate Picard constancy to #J(F₂)=25 using geometric cycle classes and Frobenius. Under constant Picard scheme and the at-most-one rational semistable-or-smooth-supersingular fiber hypothesis, prove the large-fiber, additive-fiber and uniqueness constraints. Keep the singularity assumption Δ=0 in the c₄ reduction test.

stages.title: Fourteen explicit models over F₂
stages.description: Specify and verify fourteen bounded Weierstrass models: eleven with nonzero j and three with j=0. Include the three omitted equations as separate model certificates. For each, prove global minimality, geometric rationality, all rational fiber types and splitting data, and the resolved-surface count25. Include the degree-two bad fibers of models2 and14. Generic cubic point counts alone do not certify the surface. Isomorphism classifications and exhaustiveness belong to G.6.

stages.title: Completeness and classification certificates
stages.description: Prove that every relatively minimal geometrically rational Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹_F₂ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular is equivalent to one of the fourteen candidates, under admissible Weierstrass changes and PGL₂(F₂). Separate bounded coefficient normalization and enumeration, the 512 coordinate transformations, all-place minimality, regular resolutions, rationality, component splitting and point-count certificates from the exhaustive and pairwise-distinct classification. Acquire William Lang (2000) for its configuration exclusions, or supply a complete finite certificate with a justified witness for every rejection. The classification is conditional on that certificate; the candidate equations alone do not prove it.
